name: Pennyfold's Counting-Vaults
resident: Captain Sabeline Marr and the pick of the Fair Company, and the writ-press they print their protection on
story: The Tallymen cut Pennyfold's vaults to count the south road's goods in the dry: tally-rooms, a strongroom for the fees, a lock-up for whoever argued. The Fair Company kept every room for what it was built for. The fees still go in the strongroom, the arguers still go in the lock-up, and the tally-room is where the writs are printed, sealed and entered, one line a customer.
unique_object: the Company's writ-press, a clerk's copying-press with the Tallymen's old seal still bolted in its bed, printing protection by the ream

name: The Hush Hole
resident: Ambrose Quell, the Word-Seller, and the smugglers who work his landing, with the Spire's dropouts keeping the Hush on its throat
story: A cave the Mere cut when it stood ten metres higher, going down through the fen cliff to a lake of its own and a landing where the boats come in under the cliff from the open water. Every sound in it stops a stride from where it was made. The smugglers keep their stock on the ledges, their boats at the landing, and their word-seller in the deepest hall, where the water is so still the lamps show twice.
unique_object: a landing stage of old Gullhithe jetty-planks under the cliff, with a Sedgemire punt and a Mere boat tied side by side at it

name: The Cellars under Gull Holm
resident: gutter drakes by the hundred, and the Brood-Mother on the warm stone at the bottom
story: The Builders' pier-house had cellars as deep as it was tall, for the lamp's oil and the keeper's stores, and at the bottom a light-stone set in the floor to feed the lamp: the same sul-stone the Lamp at Gullhithe burns. The pier-house fell; the stone did not go out. The drakes found its warmth and have laid round it since, and every spring the egg-collectors who land on the holm come back with one warm egg from a room with no nest in it.
unique_object: a light-stone the size of a millstone set in the floor of the lowest vault, warm to stand on, ringed with eggshell a hand deep
